report_name: Windows 11 Update KB5124008 Reportedly Breaks Always On VPN

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Publisher of the faulty Windows 11 security update KB5124008 that caused disruptions to Always On VPN functionality.

identities.name: Enterprise Organizations
identities.description: Enterprise users of Windows 11 who rely on the Always On VPN feature were impacted by the faulty KB5124008 update, which prevented remote employees from connecting to corporate networks.

indicators.name: Windows Always On VPN Connection Failure Event
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Always On VPN Connection Failure Event
id: 9b1b3c2d-8e4a-4f6b-8c1d-9a3b1c2d8e4a
status: experimental
description: Detects Windows RasClient Event ID 20227, which may indicate a failure to establish a VPN connection, potentially related to issues like the one caused by update KB5124008.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: system
detection:
  selection:
    Provider_Name: 'RasClient'
    EventID: 20227
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Windows RasClient Event ID 20227 in the System log, which indicates a failure to establish a VPN connection. This event was noted as a key indicator for troubleshooting the issues caused by the KB5124008 update.

indicators.name: Windows Update KB5124008 Uninstallation
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Update KB5124008 Uninstallation
id: f8a1b2c3-d4e5-4f6a-b7c8-d9e0f1a2b3c4
status: experimental
description: Detects the command-line uninstallation of Windows Update KB5124008, a potential remediation step for the Always On VPN issue.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
level: low
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wusa.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/uninstall'
      - '/kb:5124008'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of wusa.exe to uninstall Windows update KB5124008. This was the primary remediation step suggested for affected users to restore Always On VPN functionality.
